text: In one corner, with his head buried in his arms, sat a sailor (Max into position)
speaker: Stage

text: Near him stood two haggard women at a tawdry bar (Lucy and Cora into position)
speaker: Stage

text: A young man was lighting a long thin pipe (James into position)
speaker: Stage

text: You here, Adrian?
speaker: Dorian

text: Where else should I be? None of the chaps will speak to me now. I don't care, as long as one has opium, one doesn't want friends. I think I have had too many friends.
speaker: Adrian

text: Dorian looked round at the grotesque things with the twisted limbs, the gaping mouths, the staring lustreless eyes.
speaker: Chorus

text: He knew in what strange heavens they were suffering
speaker: Chorus

text: And what dull hells were teaching them the secret of some new joy.
speaker: Chorus

text: A woman approaches - he waves her off
speaker: Stage

text: We are very proud tonight.
speaker: Woman

text: For God's sake don't talk to me. What do you want?  Money?  Here it is.  Don't ever talk to me again.
speaker: Dorian

text: There goes the devil's bargain!
speaker: Woman

text: Curse you - don’t call me that.
speaker: Dorian

text: Prince Charming is what you like to be called, ain't it?
speaker: Woman

text: (The sailor leaps to his feet- grabs Dorian and starts to throttle him - Dorian pulls away and the sailor clicks his pistol)
speaker: Stage

text: Keep quiet. If you stir, I’ll shoot you.
speaker: Sailor

text: What have I done to you?
speaker: Dorian

text: You wrecked the life of Sibyl Vane - she was my sister.  She killed herself. I swore I would kill you in return.  For years I have sought you. I knew nothing of you but the pet name she used to call you - Prince Charming.
speaker: Sailor

text: I never knew her. I never heard of her.  You are mad.
speaker: Dorian

text: Down on your knees!
speaker: Sailor

text: Stop! How long ago is it since your sister died?
speaker: Dorian

text: Eighteen years. Why? What do years matter?
speaker: Sailor

text: Eighteen years. Set me under the lamp and look at my face!
speaker: Dorian

text: (James Vane drags him to the light)
speaker: Stage

text: You are but a boy. I would have murdered you! Forgive me, sir.  I was deceived.  A chance word set me on the wrong track.
speaker: Sailor

text: You had better go home and put that pistol away, or you may get into trouble.
speaker: Dorian

text: Why didn't you kill him? You fool!
speaker: Woman

text: He is not the man I am looking for. The man whose life I want must be nearly forty now. This one is little more than a boy.
speaker: Sailor

text: Little more than a boy!  Why, it's nigh on eighteen years since Prince Charming made me what I am.
speaker: Woman

text: You lie!
speaker: Sailor

text: Before God I am telling the truth. They say he has sold himself to the devil for a pretty face.  It's eighteen years since I met him.  He hasn't changed much since then.
speaker: Woman

text: Then he is a demon!
speaker: Sailor

text: James Vane rushed out in pursuit.
speaker: Chorus

text: Dorian crosses the stage.  Chorus form an open door using pictures as panels – Dorian passes through and closes door behind him.

text: He leans on the door and it ‘disintegrates’ and he falls.
